Hushim
HOO-shim
n. (a son of Dan, and, separately, a wife of Shaharaim of Benjamin)
Hebrew Chushim (H2366), plural form, possibly meaning "those who hasten" or "swiftness," from chush, to make haste.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Hushim is named, in Genesis’s brief account of the household that went down to Egypt with Jacob, as the whole of Dan’s recorded offspring: “And the sons of Dan; Hushim” (Genesis 46:23) — a singular name given in a plural grammatical form, most naturally read as the name of Dan’s one son who founded the entire tribe. The Chronicler preserves a variant of the same name among the descendants of Benjamin, “Shuppim also, and Huppim, the children of Ir, and Hushim, the sons of Aher” (1 Chronicles 7:12), showing the name recurring, as many Hebrew names do, across different tribal lines. A wholly separate Hushim appears two chapters later as a wife: “Shaharaim begat children in the country of Moab, after he had sent them away; Hushim and Baara were his wives” (1 Chronicles 8:8), and her own son’s line is then traced — “of Hushim he begat Abitub, and Elpaal” (1 Chronicles 8:11), the ancestor, several generations further on, of the family that produced King Saul (1 Chronicles 8:33). One name, evidently in use among both Dan’s tribe and later Benjamite households, thus threads through two of the twelve tribes’ genealogies.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Hushim; the name belongs both to the son who represents the whole tribe of Dan in Genesis 46 and, separately, to a wife of Shaharaim in the genealogy of Benjamin.

HUSHIM, n. A name borne by a son of Dan and, separately, by a wife of Shaharaim of the tribe of Benjamin.

TRIBE, n. A family, race, or series of generations descended from the same progenitor; one of the twelve divisions of Israel.

GENEALOGY, n. An account or history of the descent of persons or families from an ancestor.

PROGENITOR, n. An ancestor in the direct line; a forefather.

HOUSEHOLD, n. Those who dwell under one roof and compose a family; in Scripture, especially the covenant family unit.

Key Scripture

Genesis 46:23 — "And the sons of Dan; Hushim."

1 Chronicles 7:12 — "Shuppim also, and Huppim, the children of Ir, and Hushim, the sons of Aher."

1 Chronicles 8:8 — "And Shaharaim begat children in the country of Moab, after he had sent them away; Hushim and Baara were his wives."

1 Chronicles 8:11 — "And of Hushim he begat Abitub, and Elpaal."

Modern Corruption

A single name recurring, without confusion, across distinct tribal genealogies compiled centuries apart is the mark of careful transmission, not loose invention.

expand to see more

Source-critical approaches that treat the tribal lists of Genesis and Chronicles as independently and carelessly assembled fragments cannot easily account for the disciplined way the text keeps Dan's Hushim and Benjamin's Hushim distinct across two different books without ever conflating them — a genuinely careless compiler merges similar names; a careful transmitter of real family records keeps them straight, which is exactly what happens here.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the LORD's own care for the seventy souls who went down into Egypt (Genesis 46:27), each one named, however briefly, because each one mattered to the covenant purpose that would, four hundred years later, bring a nation back out. No name in the register, however small its later record, is there by accident.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Chushim (H2366), from chush (H2363), to make haste; ben (H1121), son; ishshah (H802), wife, woman; mishpachah (H4940), family.

expand to see more

Hebrew Chushim (H2366) — possibly those who hasten, from chush, to make haste.

Hebrew ben (H1121) — son; the word introducing Hushim in Genesis 46:23.

Hebrew ishshah (H802) — wife, woman; the Chronicler's word for the second Hushim.

Hebrew mishpachah (H4940) — family, clan; the structuring unit of both genealogies.

Hebrew yalad (H3205) — to bear, beget; the verb governing both lines of descent.

Usage

"“The sons of Dan; Hushim” — the tribe's founding representative."

"“Hushim and Baara were his wives” — a different Hushim, in Benjamin's line."

"“Of Hushim he begat Abitub, and Elpaal” — her descendants traced onward."
